about: The UN Sustainable Development Goals HAX meets, and how. Only goals with evidence are listed: the goal isn't to meet all 17, it's to show how HAX meets the ones it does. Goals 7 and 12 come from the HAX docs (the Efficient pillar page uses <un-sdg goal=7> and <un-sdg goal=12>); the rest were proposed from WORLDVIEW, the pledges and WINS and confirmed by the platform owner (2026-11-11). pillars and nodes are ids in hax-ecosystem.mmd; wins are headings in praw WINS.md. build_plans.py reads this file.

goals.name: Quality Education
targets: 4.3 equal access to affordable tertiary education
4.5 equal access, including for persons with disabilities
goals.why: Education-led, accessible and open by default, and students learn by building a real product.

goals.name: Affordable and Clean Energy
goals.why: Less energy per page: web standards over large libraries, offline-capable PWAs, caching, and services that run only when called.

goals.name: Decent Work and Economic Growth
targets: 8.6 youth in education, employment or training
goals.why: Students leave with real-product experience that carries into industry; small businesses run their own sites.

goals.name: Industry, Innovation and Infrastructure
targets: 9.c access to information and communications technology
goals.why: Open infrastructure others reuse on their own: hundreds of open web components and packages.
wins: 640+ open HTML tags, used across Penn State

goals.name: Reduced Inequalities
targets: 10.2 inclusion of all, irrespective of disability
goals.why: Access for everyone, everywhere, regardless of physical ability, technical ability or device; performance treated as access.

goals.name: Responsible Consumption and Production
goals.why: Content outlives redesigns, so nothing is rebuilt; standards replace heavy libraries and whole layers of code.
wins: Hundreds of thousands of lines removed

goals.name: Partnerships for the Goals
goals.why: Community is architecture: colleges, foundations, companies and students build HAX together.
